title: Completed marketplace orders in 2025
prompt: The marketplace team wants to know how many orders placed through the marketplace channel in 2025 actually completed (not cancelled or refunded). How many is that?
population: Orders placed on or after 2025-01-01 through the marketplace channel.
referenceSql: SELECT count(*) AS completed_orders FROM orders WHERE channel = 'marketplace' AND status = 'completed' AND order_date >= DATE '2025-01-01'

commonWrongAnswers.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE channel = 'marketplace'
commonWrongAnswers.whyWrong: Ignores the completed-status and 2025 filters, so it counts every marketplace order ever, including cancelled and refunded ones.

title: Refund rate by channel
prompt: Leadership wants to know which sales channel has the highest refund rate. For each channel, what share of orders end up refunded?
population: All orders, across all channels and dates.
metricDefinition: refunded orders / total orders, grouped by channel.
referenceSql: SELECT channel, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'refunded')::DOUBLE / count(*) AS refund_rate FROM orders GROUP BY channel

commonWrongAnswers.sql: SELECT channel, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'refunded') FROM orders GROUP BY channel
commonWrongAnswers.whyWrong: Returns the refund count, not the rate — no denominator, so channels can't be fairly compared.

title: Average order value by customer segment
prompt: Are wholesale customers placing bigger orders than retail customers, on average? Compare average order value (after discounts) by customer segment.
population: All orders with at least one order item, joined to their customer's segment.
metricDefinition: average, per order, of sum(quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount)) across its order_items, grouped by customer segment.
referenceSql: SELECT c.segment, avg(order_totals.total) AS avg_order_value FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN (SELECT order_id, sum(quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount)) AS total FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id) order_totals ON order_totals.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.segment

commonWrongAnswers.sql: SELECT c.segment, avg(oi.unit_price) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id GROUP BY c.segment
commonWrongAnswers.whyWrong: Averages line-item unit price directly, ignoring quantity and discount and mixing the order_items grain into a per-order metric — a classic grain mistake.
